gaps.quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$, so it is exact for any initial auxiliary contents.
gaps.note: The forward invocation is said to subtract x_S from y_S, which with D as X and H as Y gives H-D, but the shear replaces H by H+D; the page also never says how the u-bit address fields correspond to banks of scalars indexed by triples S, so the reader cannot reconcile the identification.

gaps.quote: A forward, inverse, forward schedule of these invocations exchanges the two banks and returns every auxiliary wire to its starting value (cited).
gaps.note: The page does not say what the inverse invocation does or between which banks each invocation runs, and three invocations from X to Y and back would not exchange the banks; nor does it say how this schedule relates to the three updates, of which it said only the middle one uses the network, so the role of this cited claim is unclear.
